Follow the video

01
00:00–01:20

Build the Form container

  1. Open the HomePage with its default AppBar and body Column.
  2. Find the Form widget in Form Elements and place it inside the page’s Column.
  3. Put a Column inside the Form so the input widgets can be stacked vertically.

Your inputs must be descendants of the Form, not siblings outside it.

02
01:20–02:40

Add the inputs and button

  1. Inside the Form’s Column, add two TextFields, one DropDown, and a Button in that order.
  2. Name the first TextField email, the second password, and the DropDown studentTeacher.
  3. Keep the button below the dropdown. The video initially uses the default labels and button text.

The screen should contain two input lines, a dropdown, and a button.

03
02:40–04:30

Explore TextField behaviour

  1. Select email and expand Additional Properties.
  2. Locate Password Field, Show Clear Field Icon, Autofocus, Autocomplete, and Auto Fill Hint.
  3. The video explores these controls and shows Autofocus enabled. Treat these as behaviour demonstrations, rather than switches that must all be enabled.

Autofocus places the cursor in a field when the page opens.

04
04:30–05:20

Explore updates while typing

  1. Locate Update Page On Change on the selected email TextField.
  2. The video temporarily enables it and demonstrates an Update Delay of 2000 milliseconds.
  3. Use this setting when the page needs to rebuild after input changes. Later video frames show it switched off again.

This is an explored option; 2000 ms is not a required final setting.

05
05:20–06:50

Configure keyboard and inspect masks

  1. Set the email TextField’s Keyboard Type to Email Address.
  2. Open Mask to inspect preset formats and the Custom option. The video also opens the Filter menu and Custom Regexp field.
  3. No completed custom mask or regular expression is visible. Leave Mask and Filter as None unless your own task requires a specific rule.

An email keyboard changes the keyboard layout; it does not by itself validate an address.

06
06:50–08:00

Inspect keyboard submit actions

  1. Locate Submit Type below the input settings.
  2. The video demonstrates keyboard action labels such as Done, Next, Previous, Send, Search, and Go using a phone preview.
  3. Choose the action appropriate for your input flow. No single final submit type is established by the demonstration.

These controls customise the keyboard action; additional app actions may still be needed.

07
By approximately 08:00

Enable password entry

  1. Select the second TextField, named password.
  2. Enable its Password Field property.
  3. Confirm that the password visibility icon appears at the right of the second field, as shown in this frame.

This screenshot also shows the dropdown options being edited; notice the password icon on the canvas.

08
08:00–08:45

Set Student and Educator options

  1. Select the studentTeacher DropDown.
  2. Under Define Options, replace the default entry with Student, then add Educator.
  3. Keep the hint as “Please select...”. The video then explores initial selection and alternative value/label configurations.

Both Student and Educator should be available in the list.

09
08:45–09:30

Explore dropdown values and labels

  1. Inspect Add Option Labels to separate stored values from the labels displayed to users.
  2. The video briefly changes the option value data type to Integer while showing Student and Educator labels.
  3. This is an exploration, not a complete final integer mapping. For the basic form, keep the simple text options from the preceding step.

Do not copy the temporary “Option 1” value into an integer field as a finished configuration.

10
09:30–10:40

Inspect Form validation

  1. Select the parent Form in the Widget Tree.
  2. Expand Validation and find email, password, and studentTeacher.
  3. Locate Automatically Validate. The video shows it off while demonstrating manual validation and field settings.

If an input is missing from the validation list, check that it is inside the Form.

11
10:40–11:50

Require the fields

  1. Enable validation for email, password, and studentTeacher.
  2. For the text inputs, inspect Error Message, Min Required Characters, Max Allowed Characters, and Text Validator.
  3. The visible required-field message is “Field is required”. The video opens the email validator choices, but later frames show None selected; it does not establish a final Email validator.

For your own app, add an Email validator if format checking is needed. That is an improvement beyond the final visible settings.

12
11:50–12:35

Style the validation errors

  1. Select the email TextField and find its input decoration settings.
  2. Inspect the error border colour and enable Custom Error Style.
  3. The frame shows an Error theme colour, border width 2, corner radius 8, and error text size 14. Use the error styling controls to make invalid input clear.

This step changes how errors look; the Form controls when validation runs.

13
12:35–13:20

Add the Validate Form action

  1. Select the Button, open Actions, and add an On Tap action.
  2. Choose Validate Form and select the Form to validate; the video’s action panel identifies it as Form_1.
  3. Open the Action Flow Editor to inspect the chain. The video adds temporary undefined actions and removes that chain as part of its exploration.

Keep a usable Validate Form action for a validation exercise; do not retain undefined action nodes.

14
13:20–14:10

Explore an action on validation error

  1. Select the Form and inspect Add Action on Error in its Validation settings.
  2. The video enables this option and explores Navigate → Navigate to Page.
  3. An onboarding template page called Onboarding1 is introduced and selected as the destination.

This navigation is attached to a validation error. It is not evidence of successful login or registration.

15
14:10–14:40

Test the demonstrated navigation

  1. Open Test mode and inspect the blank form.
  2. The video clicks the button and subsequently shows the onboarding Welcome screen.
  3. When reproducing this exploration, check the action trigger and destination yourself. For a real submission flow, show errors on invalid input and navigate only after the required successful checks.

The video’s error-action experiment should not be treated as a completed authentication flow.

16
14:40–15:20

Explore Reset Form Fields

  1. Return to the Button’s action settings. The video removes an existing action and selects Reset Form Fields.
  2. Select the email and password fields in the action panel.
  3. This is a separate action demonstration replacing the earlier button action, rather than another mandatory step in one submission chain.

Try entering sample values before testing reset so the result is visible.

17
15:20–15:35

Explore Clear Text Fields

  1. Replace the temporary reset action with Clear Text Fields.
  2. Select the email and password fields you intend to clear.
  3. The video shows the field selection controls; test the resulting action in your own project to confirm its effect.

Treat Reset and Clear as alternative demonstrations, not actions to run automatically before validation.

18
15:35–16:05

Explore Set Form Field

  1. Replace the temporary action with Set Form Field.
  2. Choose the email field.
  3. Open the Value selector to inspect sources such as Page Parameters, Global Properties, and Widget State. The video ends with this selector open; no completed value or final test is visible.

To finish your own practice, choose a suitable value and test it. This finishing task is an extension beyond the video.

Testing checklist

The following checks are suggested practice tasks. They help you verify your implementation beyond the video’s brief demonstrations.

CheckWhat to inspect
Widget hierarchyForm contains the Column, email, password, dropdown, and button.
PasswordCharacters are obscured and the visibility control behaves as expected.
DropdownStudent and Educator can be selected; the empty state shows the hint.
Required inputRun Validate Form with blank fields and inspect the required messages.
Email formatIf you add an Email validator as an extension, test an invalid address and a valid sample.
Reset / ClearTest each action separately with nonempty sample input.
Set Form FieldComplete the value selection and confirm the selected field receives that value.

For a finished submission flow: Keep validation before processing input. Use error handling to help the user correct mistakes. Configure any success navigation separately; the recording’s onboarding navigation is explored under Add Action on Error.

Prepared from the user-supplied Forms video. Screenshots are embedded in this HTML; no separate image folder is required. Review checkboxes reset when the page reloads.
